To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

non-steroid anti-inflammatory agents (NSAIDs) suppress the effects of slow-reacting substance C (SERS-C) and of arachidic acid on the resistance to perfusion to the dog hind paw, on the contractile response of strips of the rabbit aorta and the rat stomach bathed in blood obtained from an anaesthethized dog, and on the formation of rabbit aorta contracting material and prostaglandins in blood and platelet-rich plasma incubated with

SRS‐C (slow reacting substance of anaphylaxis) or arachidic acid, injected into an anaesthetised dog, or added in vitro to dog blood or to platelet‐rich dog plasma, causes the release of prostaglandin‐like substances from platelets, resulting in the generation of a contracting substance (RabAcs) for the rabbit aorta, which is suppressed by treatment of the dog with anti‐inflammatory agents.
non‐steroid antininflammatory drugs suppress the formation of a rabbit contracting substance from slow reacting substance C and arachidic acid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of a rabbit‐aorta‐contracting substance (RCS) which is generated by slow reacting substance C and which is suppressed by non‐steroid, anti‐inflammatory agents.
the generation of rabbit aorta contracting activity from SRS‐C and arachidic acid by blood, blood platelets, and soybean lipoxidases.
the generation of rabbit aorta contracting activity (RCS) from a slow reacting substance of anaphylaxis (SRS‐A) and arachidic acid in blood.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the non‐steroid drugs suppress the formation of RCS and prostaglanin from SRS‐C and arachidic acid in vitro and in vivo.
SRS‐C and arachidic acid generate RCS, which is a potent vasoconstrictor.
non‐steroid drugs suppress the formation of RCS by inhibiting prostacyclin synthetase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
non‐steroid antiphlogistics are able to inhibit the formation of RCS and prostaglanding in vivo and in vitro.
SRS‐C is a substrate for the generation of prostaglandin and RCS in vivo and in vitro.
the anti‐inflammatory effect of non‐steroid drugs is mediated by the inhibition of prostaglandin formation in the platelets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a new, simple, and rapid method for the synthesis of a wide variety of 2‐aryl‐1,3‐dioxanes.
the non‐steroid drugs inhibit the effects of SRS‐ C and arachidic acid on the hind paw of the dog, the rabbit aorta and the rat stomach.
the anti-inflammatory effects of aspirin, ibuprofen and other NSAIDs are not limited to their effects on the COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes.
